$comment: Canonical port layout + capabilities of the comparison HTTP stacks install.sh / install.ps1 set up on endpoint VMs. Guarded on every side of the seam: Rust (crates/networker-tester/src/http_stacks.rs — used by pageload/throughput/browser https→http rewrites and --http-stacks), C# (ProvisioningOrchestrator.ProxyHttpsPort — ProxyHttpsPortTests; HttpStackCatalog — embedded, served by GET /api/http-stacks + /api/modes `stacks`, drives the mode⇄target h3 gate — HttpStacksManifestTests), dashboard (lib/http-stacks.ts — http-stacks-manifest.test.ts), and lab/validate.sh (expects h3 modes only where h3 is true). `h3_modes` lists the probe modes that need HTTP/3 on the target: the gates refuse them on stacks with h3=false. The bare networker-endpoint is 8080/8443 (h3 true) and is listed as `endpoint`. Change a port here AND in the installer in the same PR.

stacks.installer: install.ps1 -Setup iis [-Fqdn] / install.sh _iis_setup_powershell <fqdn> (Windows Server 2022+; http.sys serves HTTP/3 on 8445 ONLY to clients that send TLS SNI, so the installer binds an SNI hostname listener + certificate SAN for the endpoint's DNS name — Azure public-IP DNS label / AWS public DNS (IMDS) / lab target-N.lab — and the control plane records that name as deployment.endpoint_hosts[i] (V050) and dispatches proxy runs to it instead of the IP; measured h3 2/2 through IIS in the lab's Windows target, v0.28.210)
